Reference-bank class-conditional log-likelihood for one subject

Source: R/likelihood.R
mbmm_class_loglik.Rd

Computes the class-conditional mechanistic likelihood for one subject by averaging trajectory likelihoods over a class-specific reference bank.

Usage

mbmm_class_loglik(
  obs,
  bank_pred,
  sigma,
  exclude_donor = NULL,
  donor_col = "id",
  bundle_col = "bundle_id",
  log_scale = TRUE,
  donor_weighting = c("equal", "particle")
)

Arguments

obs

This subject's observations. A data.frame containing time and y, and optionally target, censored, and lod.

bank_pred

Long-format bank predictions for one class or phenotype. Must contain the columns named by donor_col and bundle_col, together with time, pred, and optionally target.

sigma

Measurement-error SD on the Gaussian likelihood scale. Either one positive numeric value or, for multitarget data, a named numeric vector with one value for every target.

exclude_donor

Optional donor ID or vector of donor IDs to remove before scoring. Use this for leave-one-subject/donor-out scoring.

donor_col

Name of the donor column in bank_pred.

bundle_col

Name of the within-donor bundle/particle column in bank_pred.

log_scale

If TRUE, y, pred, and lod are assumed to already be on the log10 scale. If FALSE, all three are log10-transformed internally.

donor_weighting

Either "equal" or "particle". "equal" first averages particles within donor and then donors, matching the manuscript reference-bank construction. "particle" averages all donor-particle bundles together.

Value

A scalar class-conditional log-likelihood. Returns -Inf when no eligible bank draw overlaps the subject's observations.

Details

For equal donor weighting, the function first averages over the retained particles/bundles contributed by each donor and then averages across donors:

$$ L_{ik} = \frac{1}{D_k} \sum_{d=1}^{D_k} \left[ \frac{1}{M_{kd}} \sum_{m=1}^{M_{kd}} p(Y_i \mid Z_i = k, \theta_{kdm}) \right]. $$

This two-stage averaging ensures that a donor with more retained particles does not receive greater weight in the reference-bank likelihood.

Detected observations contribute a Gaussian density. Left-censored observations contribute the Gaussian probability of falling below the LOD.

Examples

obs <- data.frame(
  time = c(0, 1, 2),
  y = c(1, 2, 3)
)

close_bank <- data.frame(
  id = "donorA",
  bundle_id = 1,
  time = c(0, 1, 2),
  pred = c(1.05, 1.95, 3.1)
)

far_bank <- data.frame(
  id = "donorB",
  bundle_id = 1,
  time = c(0, 1, 2),
  pred = c(5, 5, 5)
)

mbmm_class_loglik(obs, close_bank, sigma = 0.2)
#> [1] 1.883998
mbmm_class_loglik(obs, far_bank, sigma = 0.2)
#> [1] -360.4285
